newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, allies offer new arms reductions in Europe.
newsitem.headline: France, allies offer new arms reductions in Europe.

text.p: Paris said on Thursday it planned to join other countries in offering new cuts in stocks of heavy weapons to speed negotiations on updating a 1990 treaty on conventional forces in Europe.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said France concluded in February that more cuts were impossible but decided after a second look that it could accept a reduction of around five percent within the framework of an adapted treaty.

"When the adapted treaty took effect, if it guaranteed in a satisfactory manner the security interests of all participating states, France would be willing, along with other states, to accept a reduction of its national ceilings," Rummelhardt said.
Western diplomats said the new reductions in conventional arms would be offered by NATO members in a statement to be released at a negotiating session in Vienna on Thursday.
The seven-year-old Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty is one of the key post-Cold War accords limiting numbers of weapons and where they can be placed.
NATO wants to scrap group ceilings for force levels in favour of purely national ceilings while Russia wants to retain them.
NATO also demands the right to station some foreign forces in other countries, but Russia rejects this.
Rummelhardt said France would agree to reduce its rights to 80 of 1,306 tanks, 120 of 3,820 armoured vehicles and 100 of 1,292 pieces of artillery.
The number of combat helicopters to which France would be entitled would remain unchanged, he said.
"Since February, NATO members have offered a significant reduction in their allotment rights," he said.
"This promise is today spelled out, in order to demonstrate our common will to rapidly achieve an agreement on an adaptation of the Treaty on Conventional Forces in Europe."
Rummelhardt said the ultimate success of the negotiations depended on the parties' ability to agree on an approach which guaranteed stability and greater opennness.
"The adaption of the CFE treaty must make a contribution to the new European security architecture," he said.
"We hope that an agreement resting on the basic elements of the adapted treaty can be adopted before the end of the current negotiating session on July 25."
